context.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization platform gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern Azure-based cloud platform. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining the mainframe as the system of record for three years.

## Key Elements
* **Customer / Broker**: External actors submitting claims online.
* **Claims Adjuster**: Internal users handling claims via the new web application.
* **New Claims Platform (Azure)**: Modern cloud application handling R-01 and R-02.
* **Legacy Mainframe System (On-Premises)**: 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 system of record.
* **Active Directory**: On-premises identity provider.
* **Integration Gateway**: Anti-Corruption Layer managing communication boundaries.

## Relationships
* **Customer / Broker** -> **New Claims Platform**: HTTPS for claim submission.
* **Claims Adjuster** -> **New Claims Platform**: HTTPS for adjuster web UI workflows.
* **New Claims Platform** -> **Active Directory**: OIDC/SAML for Single Sign-On.
* **New Claims Platform** <-> **Legacy Mainframe**: Asynchronous SFTP, file drops, and message queues.

## Technology Stack
* **Azure West Europe**: Cloud provider region chosen for modern managed services, accommodating the team's low cloud experience.
* **Azure Service Bus / Integration Gateway**: Asynchronous messaging to insulate the cloud platform from mainframe volatility.
* **OIDC / SAML**: Protocols for Active Directory Single Sign-On.
* **HTTPS**: Secure protocol for web and user interactions.
* **SFTP / File Transfer**: Batch-compatible protocol for legacy mainframe integration within the 23:00-05:00 window.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture safely decouples the modern Azure cloud platform from the volatile on-premises mainframe using asynchronous integration. It satisfies strict migration constraints, performance goals, and security requirements while accommodating the team's limited cloud expertise.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claim submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining synchronization with the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker: External actors submitting claims online.
* Claims Adjuster: Internal users handling claims.
* Web App Portal: React frontend hosted on Azure App Service.
* Claims API Gateway / BFF: Azure API Management and .NET Core.
* Core Claims Service: .NET Core on Azure Container Apps.
* Integration & Sync Service: Azure Service Bus and Azure Functions.
* Feature Flag / Routing Service: Azure App Configuration and .NET Core middleware.
* Claims Database: Azure SQL Database.
* Legacy Mainframe System: On-premises COBOL/DB2 system.
* Active Directory & Integration Gateway: On-premises enterprise services.

## Relationships
* Customer / Broker and Claims Adjuster access Web App Portal via HTTPS.
* Web App Portal communicates with Claims API Gateway / BFF using HTTPS.
* Claims API Gateway / BFF authenticates users via Active Directory using OIDC/OAuth2, and routes requests via gRPC/HTTPS.
* Core Claims Service persists and retrieves data from Azure SQL Database using TDS/ADO.NET.
* Integration & Sync Service communicates with the on-premises Integration Gateway via AMQP and HTTPS.
* Feature Flag / Routing Service dynamically directs claim traffic between Core Claims Service and Integration Gateway.

## Technology Stack
* React & Azure App Service: Delivers sub-2s UI loads independently of backend latency.
* .NET Core & Azure API Management: Provides robust API orchestration and security.
* Azure Container Apps: Serverless Kubernetes abstraction mitigates the team's low cloud experience.
* Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions: Asynchronous messaging guarantees transactional consistency and respects batch windows.
* Azure App Configuration: Enables the 1-day rollback requirement per claim type.
* Azure SQL Database: ACID compliance ensures no data loss during incremental migration.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the fragile on-premises mainframe while leveraging Azure's scalable services for modern frontend and backend processing. It satisfies strict consistency, performance, and maintainability requirements with minimal cloud expertise.

Web App Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premises COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform on Azure West Europe. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining data consistency and supporting rapid rollback.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker & Claims Adjuster (Users)
* Legacy Mainframe System (On-Premises System of Record)
* Active Directory (Identity Provider)
* Web App Portal (React SPA, Azure App Service)
  * Authentication Wrapper (MSAL.js)
  * Claim Submission & Routing Module
  * Adjuster Workspace Module
  * Feature Flag Client (Azure App Configuration SDK)
* Claims API Gateway / BFF (.NET Core, Azure API Management)
* Core Claims Service (.NET Core, Azure Container Apps)
* Integration & Sync Service (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions)
* Claims Database (Azure SQL Database)

## Relationships
* Customer / Broker -> Web App Portal: Accesses portal to submit claims [HTTPS]
* Claims Adjuster -> Web App Portal: Accesses portal for claim workflows [HTTPS]
* Web App Portal -> Claims API Gateway / BFF: Communicates with backend APIs [HTTPS/REST]
* Claims API Gateway / BFF -> Core Claims Service: Routes application traffic [gRPC/HTTPS]
* Core Claims Service -> Claims Database: Persists modern claims data [T-SQL]
* Integration & Sync Service -> Legacy Mainframe System: Synchronizes claim states [MQ/Batch]
* Authentication Wrapper -> Active Directory: Authenticates users via SSO [OIDC/OAuth2]

## Technology Stack
* React & Azure App Service: Delivers sub-2s SPA load times independent of backend latency.
* .NET Core & Azure Container Apps: Provides scalable microservices for claims processing.
* Azure API Management & Azure Service Bus: Secures API traffic and enables reliable asynchronous synchronization.
* Azure SQL Database & Azure App Configuration: Stores claim data and manages dynamic claim-type migrations.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the modern cloud UI and backend from high mainframe latency and expensive legacy change cycles. It uses feature flags and decoupled services to meet strict performance, security, and one-day fallback requirements.

Claims API Gateway / BFF.analysis:
## Overview
The Claims API Gateway / BFF system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy mainframe by providing secure, low-latency API orchestration and routing. It enables incremental claim type migration and sub-second adjuster screen performance via hybrid cloud deployment.

## Key Elements
- **API Router Component**: Azure API Management / .NET Core for rate limiting and token validation.
- **BFF Orchestrator Component**: .NET Core minimal API on Azure Container Apps for client data aggregation.
- **Routing Proxy Component**: .NET Core middleware for dynamic traffic splitting between modern and legacy systems.
- **Response Caching & Transformation Component**: .NET Core with Azure Cache for Redis for payload optimization.
- **External Systems**: Active Directory, Legacy Mainframe System, Integration Gateway, Web App Portal, Feature Flag / Routing Service, Core Claims Service, Claims Database.

## Relationships
- Web App Portal -> Claims API Gateway / BFF: Communicates via HTTPS/JSON.
- Claims API Gateway / BFF -> Active Directory: Authenticates users via OIDC/OAuth2.
- Claims API Gateway / BFF -> Feature Flag / Routing Service: Routes requests dynamically via gRPC/HTTPS.
- BFF Orchestrator Component -> Response Caching & Transformation Component: Uses in-process gRPC/HTTP with Azure Cache for Redis.
- Routing Proxy Component -> Integration Gateway / Core Claims Service: Directs traffic via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- **Azure API Management & Container Apps**: Selected for managed cloud infrastructure reducing cloud experience overhead.
- **.NET Core**: Chosen for robust API development, minimal APIs, and team familiarity.
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Implemented to meet sub-2s performance requirements (R-05) by caching slow mainframe responses.
- **OIDC / OAuth2 & Active Directory**: Enforced for secure enterprise single sign-on (R-07).

## Rationale
This architecture isolates legacy dependencies through explicit proxy and caching components, ensuring zero data loss during incremental migration. It guarantees sub-2s UI responses while meeting strict mainframe integration constraints.

Core Claims Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining synchronization with the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
- Customer / Broker (User)
- Claims Adjuster (User)
- Legacy Mainframe System (On-Premises System of Record)
- Active Directory (Identity Provider)
- Core Claims Service (.NET Core, Azure Container Apps)
- Claim Domain Model (Internal Component: Business logic)
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (Internal Component: Format translation)
- Outbox Processor (Internal Component: Reliable message queuing)
- Dual-Write / Sync Coordinator (Internal Component: State synchronization)

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Web App Portal: Submits claims [HTTPS]
- Claims Adjuster -> Web App Portal: Manages claims [HTTPS]
- Web App Portal -> Claims API Gateway: Forwards API requests [REST/HTTPS]
- Claims API Gateway -> Core Claims Service: Routes requests [gRPC/HTTPS]
- Claim Domain Model -> Mainframe ACL: Delegates unmigrated types [Internal C# Interface]
- Claim Domain Model -> Outbox Processor: Persists events [EF Core / TDS]
- Outbox Processor -> Integration & Sync Service: Publishes events [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
- Mainframe ACL -> Integration Gateway: Sends legacy updates [REST/HTTPS]
- Web App Portal -> Active Directory: Authenticates users [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps: Serverless Kubernetes abstraction reducing cloud complexity for the team
- .NET Core / C#: Core runtime for the modern claims microservices and domain model
- Azure Service Bus: AMQP messaging broker ensuring reliable, asynchronous event delivery
- Azure SQL Database: Relational storage for modern claim records via TDS/ADO.NET

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture uses an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous outbox pattern to safely isolate the new platform from legacy mainframe latency and costly interface constraints. This ensures zero data loss, supports incremental claim type migration, and allows a one-day rollback capability.

Integration & Sync Service.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform using a hybrid cloud approach. It gradually replaces the legacy mainframe system while maintaining synchronous data consistency.

## Key Elements
- **Sync Orchestrator Function**: .NET 8 isolated durable functions coordinating claim state synchronization.
- **Mainframe Adapter Component**: .NET 8 component managing protocol translation.
- **Outbox Event Publisher**: .NET 8 component consuming Azure Service Bus topics.
- **Idempotency & Deduplication Filter**: .NET 8 middleware validating message uniqueness against Azure SQL.
- **Integration Gateway**: On-premises gateway interfacing with the legacy mainframe.

## Relationships
- *Sync Orchestrator* -> *Outbox Event Publisher*: Dispatches messages via **Azure Service Bus [AMQP]**.
- *Sync Orchestrator* -> *Idempotency & Deduplication Filter*: Validates message uniqueness via **In-memory / gRPC**.
- *Mainframe Adapter* -> *Integration Gateway*: Sends transactional payloads via **HTTPS [REST/JSON]** using mutual TLS (mTLS).

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Functions (.NET 8)**: Chosen for serverless scalability despite team's low cloud experience.
- **Azure Service Bus [AMQP]**: Chosen for reliable asynchronous messaging and batch window isolation.
- **Azure SQL Database**: Used for idempotency state storage ensuring exactly-once processing.
- **HTTPS [REST/JSON] with mTLS**: Ensures secure and standardized hybrid-cloud transport.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture enables gradual, risk-mitigated migration of claim types while strictly adhering to legacy mainframe constraints. Robust messaging and deduplication patterns guarantee absolute consistency and prevent data loss during the transition.

Feature Flag / Routing Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Feature Flag / Routing Service dynamically directs claim traffic between a modern Azure platform and an on-premise mainframe. It ensures seamless incremental migration and rapid rollbacks for the Insurance Claims Modernization system.

## Key Elements
* Routing Engine Component (.NET Core)
* Configuration Cache Component (Azure App Configuration SDK with local JSON fallback)
* Audit & Telemetry Component (.NET Core / Application Insights)
* Circuit Breaker Component (.NET Polly)

## Relationships
* Claims API Gateway / BFF -> Routing Engine: Invokes routing via gRPC/HTTPS
* Routing Engine -> Configuration Cache: Reads dynamic rules via in-memory lookup
* Routing Engine -> Audit & Telemetry Component: Emits telemetry asynchronously via .NET Channel/Queue
* Routing Engine -> Core Claims Service / Integration & Sync Service: Directs claim traffic via gRPC/HTTPS
* Circuit Breaker -> Legacy Mainframe System: Reroutes traffic on failure via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* .NET Core: Ensures team alignment and high-performance execution.
* Azure App Configuration with local JSON fallback: Guarantees fast flag evaluation and offline resilience.
* .NET Polly: Provides automated circuit breaking and failover.
* Application Insights: Tracks routing audit trails and telemetry.

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces the 1-day rollback and zero-data-loss constraints by decoupling routing logic from business services. It mitigates cloud inexperience and latency risks through robust local caching and automated circuit breaking.

Claims Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform on Azure West Europe. It enables online claim submission, adjuster processing, and incremental claim type migration while maintaining system stability and data consistency.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customer, Broker, Claims Adjuster
- **External Systems**: Legacy Mainframe System (COBOL/DB2, On-Premises), Active Directory, Integration Gateway
- **Containers**: Web App Portal (React, Azure App Service), Claims API Gateway / BFF (.NET Core, Azure API Management), Core Claims Service (.NET Core, Azure Container Apps), Integration & Sync Service (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions), Feature Flag / Routing Service (.NET Core, Azure App Configuration), Claims Database (Azure SQL Database)
- **Claims Database Components**: Claim Repository Component (.NET Entity Framework Core), Audit & Reconciliation Component (Azure SQL Stored Procedures/Change Tracking), Migration Schema Versioning Component (FluentMigrator), Temporal History & Rollback Component (Azure SQL System-Versioned Temporal Tables)

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Web App Portal: Submits claims [HTTPS / TLS]
- Claims Adjuster -> Web App Portal: Handles claims [HTTPS / TLS]
- Web App Portal -> Claims API Gateway / BFF: Routes API requests [HTTPS / REST]
- Claims API Gateway / BFF -> Core Claims Service: Forwards domain operations [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Core Claims Service -> Integration & Sync Service: Publishes migration sync events [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
- Integration & Sync Service -> Legacy Mainframe System: Syncs records [MQ / Batch]
- Core Claims Service -> Claim Repository: Invokes data access [In-Process / C# Method Calls]
- Claim Repository -> Azure SQL Storage Engine: Executes queries [TDS / TCP 1433]
- Claim Repository -> Temporal History Component: Manages row versions [In-Process / T-SQL]
- Audit & Reconciliation Component -> Claim Repository: Reads state snapshots [In-Process / LINQ]
- Web App Portal / Core Claims Service -> Active Directory: Handles single sign-on [OIDC / OAuth2 / LDAPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Azure SQL Database**: Provides native ACID compliance and temporal tables to guarantee zero data loss (R-04) and support one-day rollbacks (R-06).
- **.NET Core & Entity Framework Core**: Powers robust backend services and relational data access with low maintenance overhead for a cloud-inexperienced team.
- **Azure Container Apps & App Service**: Host microservices and web apps natively on Azure.
- **Azure Service Bus**: Handles asynchronous messaging for hybrid integration.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive-to-change mainframe while modernizing claim types incrementally via Azure. Native cloud database features minimize custom application logic for data consistency and rollbacks, fitting a team with limited cloud experience.
